01.reason: A gentile announces Hasa drowned, Rav Nahman reacts, and Hasa's wife remarries: an incident with a response and a ruling.

02.reason: A certain man appraised orphans' coral for himself, it appreciated, and he came before Rabbi Ammi who ruled: incident followed by ruling.

03.reason: The bar Shatya case is cited as a legal precedent with conflicting testimony and competing rulings; too little of the incident is narrated.

04.reason: Two men were derided as sons of Arameans and rabbis responded with rulings; all speech, but with conflict.

05.reason: Rabbi Evyatar meets Elijah and learns of God's view of his interpretation; segment 2 is exegesis framing the encounter.

06.reason: Rava and Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak see Rav Nahman bar Ya'akov pass in a carriage, react differently, and go to him; he uncovers his arm and remarks on the wind.

07.reason: A man betrothed a woman with myrtle in the market; the case was sent to Rav Yosef who ordered him flogged and a get required.

08.reason: A husband gave his first wife's maidservant to his second wife; she cried out before Rava, who ignored her. The Gemara's explanation follows.

09.reason: Mar Ukva's habitual charity is followed by a one-time event: the pauper chases them, they hide in a furnace, and his wife explains her merit.

10.reason: Rabbi Yehuda bars Rabbi Meir's students, Sumakhos pushes in, Rabbi Yehuda grows angry and Rabbi Yosei responds.

11.reason: Nehunya's daughter falls into a cistern, Rabbi Hanina ben Dosa announces her rescue, and she is saved; segment 4 is later commentary.

12.reason: Rabbi Tzadok is propositioned by a noblewoman and climbs into the lit oven to escape; she reacts.

13.reason: A widow's son asks two rabbis questions and Rabbi Yehoshua answers him with sarcasm: mostly speech, with some conflict.

14.reason: Parents argue over whom their daughter should marry; the wife forces the husband to agree, and during the meal his relative betroths the girl on the roof.

15.reason: A man studied twelve years and came back to find his wife infertile; Rabbi deliberates, the husband prays and she is healed.

16.reason: A man deposited silk with Rav Dimi, who died without instructions; the claimant came before Rabbi Abba, who ruled.

17.reason: A man testified before Rabbi Ami that someone was a priest; after questioning him, Rabbi Ami elevated that person to priestly status.

18.reason: Rabbi Tarfon's habitual service to his mother leads to a one-time event: he boasts in the study hall and is rebuked.

19.reason: Yeimar bar Hashu sends an agent to seize a dead debtor's boat; two rabbis meet the agent and challenge the seizure.

20.reason: A report that the Galileans bought a pauper meat every day: a practice with no one-time event, followed by discussion.

21.reason: Rabbi Zeira finding Rabbi Asi teaching only frames how a ruling was transmitted; nothing happens.

22.reason: A man took a Torah scroll in the synagogue and gave it to his wife as her get; Rav Yosef rules on the case.

23.reason: An exegetical derivation of the dates of Moses' death and birth; nothing is narrated.

24.reason: An exchange of letters on a halakhic argument; speech only, with no real conflict or event.

25.reason: On his deathbed Rabbi summons the Sages, they come in, and he gives his final instructions: part of the narrative of his death.
